coveragePolicy.reason: The first novel-domain capture supplied only one course group per domain. This additive campaign partitions the same thirty-four non-holdout source kernels across two further pedagogically distinct course contexts per domain, reaching three measured groups per domain while testing the stricter v2 authoring policy on the same concepts.

groups.title: Anatomy Homeostasis and Tissues Diagnostic Lab
groups.courseBrief: Anatomy Homeostasis and Tissues Diagnostic Lab, a five-session course in which students move from levels of organization and feedback regulation to tissue classification and skin structure through short diagnostic decisions grounded in supplied claims.
groups.qualityFocus: Require students to distinguish organizational levels, negative and positive feedback, tissue categories, and epidermal versus dermal structure. Keep every causal statement inside the supplied mechanism and make each distractor a plausible nearby category rather than an invented clinical claim.

groups.title: Anatomy Movement and Signaling Case Studio
groups.courseBrief: Anatomy Movement and Signaling Case Studio, a five-session course in which students interpret joint structure, muscle categories, nervous tissue, sensory processing, and endocrine signaling through bounded structure-function cases.
groups.qualityFocus: Separate joint components from movement outcomes, muscle categories from locations, sensory transduction from perception, and hormone transport from target-cell response. Explanations must identify the decisive supplied feature and explicitly correct one nearest-neighbor misconception.

groups.title: Economics Markets and Choice Decision Lab
groups.courseBrief: Economics Markets and Choice Decision Lab, a six-session course in which students reason about demand, elasticity, equilibrium, inflation feedback, consumer choice, and model assumptions using small evidence-bounded decisions.
groups.qualityFocus: Keep movements distinct from shifts, elasticity distinct from slope, equilibrium distinct from fairness, and model conclusions distinct from assumptions. Any numerical or policy inference must be licensed by the source claims, and distractors should reflect one identifiable economic misconception.

groups.title: Economics Evidence, Flows, and Measurement Studio
groups.courseBrief: Economics Evidence, Flows, and Measurement Studio, a six-session course in which students evaluate natural experiments, circular flows, accumulation, proxy measures, labor-force classifications, and opportunity costs.
groups.qualityFocus: Stress causal comparability, stock versus flow, proxy versus construct, unemployment versus nonparticipation, and explicit opportunity cost. Questions must remain answerable from supplied claims alone and explanations must rule out the strongest tempting alternative without adding policy facts.

groups.title: Physics Charge, Fields, and Potential Workshop
groups.courseBrief: Physics Charge, Fields, and Potential Workshop, a six-session qualitative-reasoning course covering charge, electric fields, Gauss's law, potential, capacitance, and current with source-bounded representations.
groups.qualityFocus: Separate field from force, flux from field magnitude, potential from potential energy, stored charge from capacitance, and charge motion from current. Avoid invented quantities; each keyed answer must follow uniquely from the supplied relationship, sign, or representation.

groups.title: Physics Circuits, Magnetism, and Induction Lab
groups.courseBrief: Physics Circuits, Magnetism, and Induction Lab, a six-session course in which students reason qualitatively about resistance, DC circuits, magnetic fields and forces, Faraday induction, and inductance.
groups.qualityFocus: Keep resistance distinct from resistivity, circuit rules distinct from component definitions, magnetic field distinct from magnetic force, and flux change distinct from stored inductive energy. Explanations must name the decisive source relation and correct exactly one nearby misconception.

claimBoundary: This campaign measures a versioned authoring-policy change and adds two real course contexts per novel domain. Reusing the same semantic kernels supports controlled prompt-policy comparison; it is not new conceptual coverage and supplies no preference label or adapter win.
